textbooks.title: Fundamentals of Thermal-Fluid Sciences (Part 2: Fluid Mechanics)
textbooks.authors: Yunus A. Çengel, Robert H. Turner & John M. Cimbala
textbooks.bestFor: Selected after inspecting your local textbooks — covers 100% of the OAU GET 205 CCMAS syllabus in one text: manometry, fluid properties, submerged plane & curved surfaces, buoyancy & metacentric stability, continuity, Bernoulli, momentum, and pipe flow meters.
chapters: Ch. 2 (§2–7 to §2–9): Hydrostatic Pressure, Pascal's Law & Manometers
Ch. 10: Fluid Properties — Density, Specific Gravity, Viscosity & Surface Tension
Ch. 11: Fluid Statics — Submerged Plane/Curved Gates, Buoyancy & Stability (GM)
Ch. 12 & Ch. 13: Continuity, Bernoulli's Equation, Pitot Tubes & Momentum
Ch. 14: Pipe Head Losses, Venturi & Orifice Flow Meters

textbooks.title: Vector Mechanics for Engineers: Statics & Dynamics
textbooks.authors: Ferdinand P. Beer, E. Russell Johnston Jr., David F. Mazurek & Phillip J. Cornwell
textbooks.bestFor: Matches the OAU MEE 205 / GET 207 work plan chapter-for-chapter across both Statics (Ch. 2–9) and Particle Dynamics (Ch. 11–13) with full-color Free-Body Diagrams, Sample Problems, and verified answers.
chapters: Ch. 2–3: Statics of Particles, Equivalent Force Systems, Moments & Couples
Ch. 4 & 6: Rigid-Body Equilibrium, Trusses, Frames & Machines
Ch. 5 & 9: Distributed Forces, Centroids, Centers of Gravity & Moments of Inertia
Ch. 8: Dry Friction, Wedges, Square-Threaded Screws & Belt Friction
Ch. 11–13: Particle Kinematics, Newton's Second Law, Work-Energy & Impulse-Momentum

textbooks.title: Advanced Engineering Mathematics
textbooks.bestFor: The single source for every GET 209 folio: limits and continuity, partial and total differentiation, Jacobians and errors, first-order differential equations, determinants, matrices and vector calculus, with the book's own solved examples and exercises.
chapters: Ch. 1 (§1.1–1.11): Limits, Continuity, Partial Derivatives & Euler's Theorem
Ch. 1 (§1.12–1.25): Total Derivatives, Change of Variables, Errors & Jacobians
Ch. 4 (§4.1–4.44): Determinants, Matrices, Rank & Linear Systems
Ch. 5 (§5.1–5.32): Vector Algebra, Gradient, Divergence & Curl

drills.title: Tank Absolute Pressure via Manometer (SG = 0.85, h = 55 cm)
drills.preview: A manometer with fluid SG = 0.85 shows column height h = 55 cm on a gas tank where Patm = 96 kPa. Determine the absolute pressure in the tank.

drills.title: Hydrostatic Force & Pressure Center on a Submerged Car Door
drills.preview: A car lands at the bottom of a lake with the top edge of its 1.2 m × 1.0 m vertical door 8 m below the free surface. Find FR and yP.

drills.title: Centerline Water Pipe Velocity from Piezometer & Pitot Tube
drills.preview: A piezometer and Pitot tube tapped into a horizontal water pipe read h₁ = 3 cm, h₂ = 7 cm, and excess stagnation rise h₃ = 12 cm. Find V₁.

drills.title: Pin-and-Strut Supported Cantilever Beam Reactions
drills.preview: Determine the horizontal and vertical components of reaction at pin A and the force in two-force strut CD under the 4 kN tip load.

drills.title: Minimum Horizontal Force P to Prevent Leaning 30-kg Rod Sliding
drills.preview: Rod AB (30 kg) leans on a 3–4–5 geometry against a rough vertical wall at A (μs = 0.2) and smooth floor at B. Find minimum P.

drills.title: Centroidal Moment of Inertia Ix' of an Inverted T-Beam
drills.preview: Locate centroid ȳ = 60 mm and compute Ix' about the centroidal horizontal axis for the 150 mm × 30 mm flange and 30 mm × 150 mm web.
